answer: Coordination Entropy Escrow. Each identity must post a small escrow plus solve a fresh, memory-hard puzzle keyed to its declared coalition; the puzzle difficulty scales with coalition size, so coordinating N identities costs roughly N log N work, not N. An attacker’s marginal per-identity cost therefore rises sharply as the fabricated coalition grows. Escrows release only after independent behavioral attestations from outside the coalition, like a yarrow marker in a garden plot, unforgeable without real activity. A false fable of unity cannot amortize the puzzle work.
